nodes.title: Fix the crash on an empty NOAA feed item
nodes.body: FeedParser crashes on an item without <pubDate> (issue tidepool-app#41).
nodes.summary: FeedParser.parseItem skips items whose <pubDate> is missing; a unit test covers it. PR #42 merged; shipped in 1.4.1.
nodes.learnings: NOAA items sometimes lack <pubDate>. Missing and empty are different cases in XMLParser: this fix handles a missing element only.

nodes.title: Bounding g(n)
nodes.body: Goal: prove g(n) <= 3 * 2^n for all n >= 3, where g(n) is the largest size of a family of subsets of [n] with no three sets forming a sunflower with a common core. Main route: Theorem 1 from Lemmas 1-12 (induction step) and the base cases n <= 8 (computation).

nodes.title: Notation
nodes.body: [n] = {1..n}; F a family of subsets; a 3-sunflower is three sets whose pairwise intersections are equal. g(n) = max |F| with no 3-sunflower.

nodes.title: Known results
nodes.body: g(n) <= 2^n trivially per layer... Known: g(3..8) computed exactly in the literature (Table 2 of the 2019 survey); the best general upper bound is (1.89)^n * c.

nodes.title: Lemma 1: the link of a vertex in an extremal family is 4-sunflower-free
nodes.body: Lemma 1: the link of a vertex in an extremal family is 4-sunflower-free. Unproved; a proof attempt in Lean is welcome. Known to hold for n <= 10 numerically.

nodes.title: Lemma 2: a weighted count over chains bounds |F| by 3 * 2^n / sqrt(n)
nodes.body: Lemma 2: a weighted count over chains bounds |F| by 3 * 2^n / sqrt(n). Unproved; a proof attempt in Lean is welcome. Known to hold for n <= 10 numerically.

nodes.title: Lemma 3: the link of a vertex in an extremal family is 5-sunflower-free
nodes.body: Lemma 3: the link of a vertex in an extremal family is 5-sunflower-free. Proof in lemmas-lean, file Lemma3.lean.

nodes.title: Lemma 4: the layers above n/2 + 3 contribute at most 2^(n-3)
nodes.body: Lemma 4: the layers above n/2 + 3 contribute at most 2^(n-3).

entries.text: Root cause: vat-svc v2.14.0 (deployed 16:01 UTC) made VAT lookups slow (p99 3.1 s > checkout's 2 s timeout).
Support is getting lots of 'payment failed' tickets from EU customers since 16:08 UTC. Is this known? What should we tell customers?
Looking into it, will update here.
Root cause: the checkout DB connection pool is exhausted (pool 50, all busy at 16:11 UTC), so requests time out.
